article.text: ChatGPT builds text one word at a time from left to right. This is autoregressive generation along a left-to-right trajectory. Each new word extends what came before.

The same prompt does not guarantee the same output. One run can yield `and brings prosperity for all to see, embraces power` and another can yield `AI is power to grow, ignorance also learn prosperity awaits`. The difference illustrates the probabilistic nature of the system.

For any single prompt the system samples from a probability distribution to produce a reply. Many such interactions are indexed on websites with famous examples, which makes the variability observable and testable.
You can now expect variation and plan for it. Run the same prompt multiple times to sample the distribution, compare outputs, and decide when to resample, constrain, or accept a reply.

article.text: The alignment pipeline is multi-step: supervised fine-tuning, then preference ranking, then reward modeling, then policy-gradient fine-tuning. ChatGPT follows this as `Step1 Collect demonstration data and train supervised policy (SFT), Step2 Collect comparison data and train reward model (RM), Step3 Optimize policy against reward model using PPO with reward r_k` and is fine-tuned from GPT-3.5 series finished early 2022 on Azure AI supercomputing infrastructure.

Step one focuses the model on documents with the desired format, for example expecting a complete answer rather than a question at the top. Very large models are very sample efficient during this fine-tuning.

Step two generates multiple responses and has different raters rank them for preference as to which one is better. A different network is then trained as a reward model to predict how much any candidate response would be desirable.

Once the reward model exists it is used with a form of policy gradient, referred to as ELO, to further fine-tune the model. In the ChatGPT instantiation this is Proximal Policy Optimization against the reward model.

You can now decide where to invest effort for alignment: collect high-quality demonstrations for SFT, collect ranked comparisons to train a reward model, and then optimize the policy against that reward model with PPO.

article.text: The decoder-only Transformer from the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" is the same design that powers GPT-3, only much smaller. GPT-3 is basically identical in design but between 10,000 and 1 million times bigger depending on how size is counted.
